content:
Since the launch of the iPhone 4 bumper case, bumper cases have always been a favourite among Apple fans, but in recent years the choices on the market have been dwindling. For those seeking a minimalist protective case, Rhinoshield offers a rather impressive option.

Apple made a return to the bumper case market last year with the iPhone Air. I was hoping Apple would extend its bumper case to the iPhone 18 Pro (just as they did with the clear case for the iPhone 11), but unfortunately that did not come to pass. In my search for alternatives, I came across Rhinoshield's Minimalist Impact Bumper case.

Key Details

The fit of the Impact Bumper case is similar to most bumpers, with shallower protection around the screen edge and a slightly raised back edge. The case has one unique design feature that I particularly like: a special support structure that keeps the camera plateau and lenses from making direct contact with whatever surface the phone is placed on. Given that both the 17 Pro and 18 Pro feature aluminium bodies, this is especially important to me. This makes its protection far superior to typical bumper cases, and also solves that annoying wobble problem when using the phone on a flat surface.

That said, the fit of this case is not ideal. It's slightly loose, with edges that can be easily pried outward, and I worry the edges might stretch out over time. Even so, I don't think the phone will fly out of the case if dropped (I have accidentally tested this). However, the entire case is made of hard plastic rather than rubber, so I hope it holds up well over the long term. Rhinoshield states that the entire case is made from a single material, making it 100% recyclable.

The case comes in three colour options to match the iPhone 18 Pro body colours: white, blue, and black (those with the burgundy model will be disappointed). I have the blue version, which is close to but not exactly the Glacier tone.

Drawbacks

However, this case does have some drawbacks. My biggest complaint is that the buttons are very hard to press. For some reason, they went with a design that sits almost flush with the body, and combined with the button construction, the feel is mushy and imprecise.

The overall material choice may also be another drawback. To me, it feels cheaper than Apple's iPhone Air bumper, though some may actually prefer this texture. I personally prefer this material over the typical TPU/rubber clear case material. However, this material combined with the looser design seems particularly prone to picking up lint from pockets.

If you use Apple's Wrist Strap or Crossbody Strap, note that this case does not have the required lanyard attachment points.

Conclusion

The Rhinoshield bumper case is far from perfect, and I still hope Apple will extend its bumper case to other iPhone models. Ultimately, however, I decided to stick with this case, primarily because it allows me to enjoy an experience close to using no case at all, without worrying about damaging or scratching the fragile aluminium body. As far as I know, this bumper case is usually only available on their official website, priced at around US$30, which with shipping comes out to roughly the same as Apple's (US$39). You can purchase the Rhinoshield Minimalist Impact Bumper case here. (An Amazon listing appears occasionally, so you might also try to grab it there.)
